Zone - Hytale Wiki Zone From Hytale Wiki Jump to navigation Jump to search Concept art of the four zones and their undergrounds. A zone is a unique, procedural generated area in Hytale. Each zone is home to different factions and has several regions, which are made up of biomes. Each zone is centered around a different elemental magic. Orbis Zones There are currently 4 zones available in Orbis. They are intended to be processed in order to have a smooth progression, but nothing prevents the player from exploring them in different order. 2 others zone were teased in a concept art, but never shown or revealed. Emerald Wilds The Emerald Wilds, also called Zone 1, is where the player begins when starting a new adventure. It is a serene and peaceful environment with a vast amount of foliage and greenery, built to ease the player into the game's mechanics. This zone represents the Earth element, and is home to the Kweebec and Trork factions. Regions Drifting Plains Seedling Woods The Fens Factions Kweebec Trork Howling Sands The Howling Sands, also called Zone 2, is an arid environment, with very little vegetation, akin to a vast desert. Represented by the Wind element, this zone is home to the Scarak and Feran factions. Regions Golden Steppes Badlands Desolate Basin Factions Scarak Feran Whisperfrost Frontiers The Whisperfrost Frontiers, also called Zone 3, is a much colder and snowy zone, with large mountains and taiga forests. This zone represents the Water element. It holds the Outlander and Faun factions. Regions Frostmarch Tundra Boreal Reach The Everfrost Frozen Coasts Factions Outlander Faun Devastated Lands The Devastated Lands, also called Zone 4, is a hellish and barren environment devastated long ago. Scorched stone dominates the land, with lava rivers and lakes covering the surface. Zone 4 embodies the Fire element, and is home to the Slothian faction. Regions Basalt Peninsula Cinder Wastes Charred Woodlands Factions Slothian Saurian Other zone-like areas The Deep Ocean is a pseudo-Zone, distinct from other zones, having previously been described by the developers as "a zone all by itself"[1] within the game. Blocks are usually cube shaped units which make up the world of Hytale, although some have different shapes and can even take up multiple blocks. They can be mined for various materials. A lot of blocks can be mined by hand, but some require a specific tool, or can only be mined in creative mode. The speed that certain blocks can be mined depends on the type or material of the tool. As an alternative to mining, some blocks, like rubble or crops, are able to be picked up by pressing the interact key and may drop something different than if the block was mined. Types According to the creative inventory, there are eight types of blocks. TypeTool Tools refer to any device or object that is used to carry out a particular function. They can be found or crafted with materials within and around the world of Orbis. Pickaxes Pickaxes refer to a type of tool used to mine blocks. Having a higher tier pickaxe increases mining speed, durability, and allows the player to mine more kinds of blocks. Hatchets Hatchets, like pickaxes, are a type of tool used to mine blocks; however, they are mainly used to cut down trees. They can also be used as offensive weapons. Hoes Hoes refer to a type of tool used to till soil. This allows crops to grow on its surface. Currently, it is unknown whether they have any other purpose. Shovels Shovels are used to effectively mine soil blocks. Hytale Wiki:Wiki rules From Hytale Wiki Jump to navigation Jump to search See also: Style guide The Hytale Wiki is an online community resource about Hytale and related subjects. Everyone is welcome to edit the wiki. To ensure the Wiki is kept clean, concise, formal and accurate, please read the following rules. 1\. Always follow the Hytale EULA and ToS Adding any content breaching these is strictly forbidden. 2\. Vandalism Don't vandalize wiki pages. If we notice you intentionally messing up pages, you may get banned from contributing to the wiki. 3\. Advertisements Do not put any advertisements or links to your services or other communities onto the wiki pages. If you want to collaborate with us and you think your community/service would be a good fit or useful for the wiki, contact the admins. 4\. Copyright Do not upload copyrighted media that is not compatible with the wiki's license. Link the source and give proper attribution to the original author when uploading new media to the wiki. 5\. Discussion Pages Please try to use the talk pages or discuss it in out Discord to avoid edit wars. Stay on topic and discuss the page in question. 6\. External Links & References Only links to the following are allowed: Official Hytale websites, socials and media sites connected to or officially endorsed by the Hytale developers community content specifically made for the wiki (e.g. tutorial videos) and approved by the wiki admins. References made on wiki pages should consist of official information relayed by the Hytale developers. 7\. Userspace Content in userspaces must not represent itself as official or mainspace content. You may link to your socials, websites or projects you are part of or interested in. No direct download links or linking to malicious websites. 8\. Use of AI Mass-generated content or AI spam is not allowed. 9\. Follow Weird Gloop ToS 10\. Breaking the rules Breaking the rules may result in a warning, temporary ban or permanent exclusion from contributing to this wiki. Ban evasion may lead to being permanently blocked. Hytale Wiki:Style guide From Hytale Wiki Jump to navigation Jump to search This article is a stub. You can help by expanding it.Instructions: Section about rendering guideliens missing This article aims to provide a comprehensive style guide for all Hytale Wiki articles to follow. Although Wikipedia already provides a more general style guide, a more specific one is necessary for Hytale-specific guidelines. As such, only guidelines pertaining to the Hytale Wiki and its basic formatting rules should be included here. Notability Shortcut Hytale Wiki:Notability Articles are only allowed in the main namespace (the "mainspace") if they fit the following criteria. Articles which do not fit the following criteria will be deleted. Articles must be longer than a few sentences. Articles which do not meet this criteria should be merged into related articles. Articles must be directly related to Hytale in some way, whether it be about gameplay or of other directly relevant information. Redirects Redirects are exempt from the normal notability, but must redirect to an article that fits the notability guidelines. The following lists what is allowed: Alternative spellings (Armour→Armor) Excludes incorrect spelling, typos, and irregular formatting. Shortened names (Simon→Simon Collins-Laflamme, HMM→Hytale Model Maker) Plural form, but only if the target page is commonly used as a plural noun (Kweebecs→Kweebec, as they are usually referred to as a group, but not Cobblestones→Cobblestone) From a niche topic to a page about a broader topic (Warrior → Skeleton) Redirects in the user namespace may lead anywhere, except to an article that does not exist or another redirect. Titles and headers All article names and headings should: Use sentence case, but capitalize proper nouns. For example, List of factions in Hytale, not List Of Factions In Hytale. Don't use superfluous names (don't contain a, the), or self-references (Their appearance). Be singular (Kweebec not Kweebecs). Images All images uploaded to the wiki should: Use the name as seen in-game (when applicable) Use the following naming format: item name.png - Crafting Icons item name (model).png - Renders item name (equipped).png - Equipped images item name (dropped).png - Dropped Images Don't upload using a different format as a way to bypass override restrictions. For example item name(1).png to bypass overide restriction for item name.png Guides to making different renders can be found at Help:ISO. Layout Shortcut Hytale Wiki:LAYOUT All pages should be consistently laid out in the following order. Generic layout Notice templates (amboxes like {{stub}} or {{split}}) Infobox (using an infobox template) Dablinks ({{about}}, etc) Lead An opening description of the subject, summarising the page's contents, with the first instance of the page title in bold. Sections: ... Specific sections relating to the subject. Will differ between pages. History Using the {{History}} template, shows the history of the subject, documenting changes between versions. Trivia Any other useful information that doesn't fit into the other sections. Gallery Images relating to the subject, inside  tags. See also Similar articles to the page topic. References Lists references to verify the information on the page – should contain just {{reflist}}. External links Any relevant external websites relating to the topic. Navigation template(s). The most relevant topics to the page. If a page uses a navigation template, that page should usually be linked from the template, and vice versa. Categories Insert relevant categories here; note that they are usually automatically added by the infobox and navigation templates. Interwikis Blocks and items Articles about blocks and items should have the following sections, in the place of the "..." in the general layout above: Types Describes different variations or types of the item, what each type looks like, and what it possessed with. Obtaining How the block or item can be obtained, such as from finding it in the world or from crafting, etc. Usage What the block or item can be used for, whether it be crafting, consumption, etc. NPCs Articles about NPCs should have the following sections, in the place of the "..." in the general layout above: Types Describes different variations or types of the creature, what each type looks like, and what they wear and wield. Habitat Describes the habitat or location where the creature lives. Include alterverse and zone. Life cycle The creature may differ as it grows older. List the changes here. Behavior Describes how the creature acts and behaves in-game. Drops What items the NPC drops when it dies. Backstory Describes the story line of the creature that took place prior to the events in Hytale. Other articles Since the game is not out yet and not all information is known about the subjects of pages, please use your best judgement when laying out articles. Place the most important information nearer to the top for readers to find more easily. Writing The Hytale Wiki's purpose is to document facts about the game, so articles should avoid speculation and unsourced information. If information is obvious or can be found in-game, it does not need a reference, but if it is a quote, relation to a real-world object, or some other lesser known fact that a citation should be added. If a feature is mentioned to be added in an upcoming update, it must be adequately sourced. Articles in the mainspace should always be written in third-person and without terms referring to the reader. Also avoid abbreviations or contractions. When emphasis is needed, italics (using wikimarkup; ''italic text'') should be used, not boldface or CAPITALS. Tutorial information should not be contained in regular articles. Information relating to mods should not be contained on articles relating to the base game. Mods should also not be linked from articles not about mods. Lead section The lead section, also sometimes referred to as the article introduction, should align their initial identification of the content using the singular or plural form of the article's title. For example, in zone, the lead begins with the following, "A zone is a unique, procedural generated area in Hytale." In this case, zones are referred to the singular form, as they can be described in singular form. However, in the case of an article with a plural title such as Copper Daggers, the following can be used, "Copper Daggers are a two-handed melee weapon with a rarity of Common." In extraordinary circumstances, the community may discuss and determine that a particular article may use a different form to its title due to the nature of its contents. An example would be the Minigame article being described as Minigames within its lead section. Language Shortcut Hytale Wiki:LANGUAGE Use American English when writing, as this is the variant of English Hytale.com uses. Do not use IDs for the basis of title articles, as they do not reflect the names appropriately. Dates Dates should be spelled out in full, with no additional punctuation (e.g., either "January 10, 2026" or "10 January 2026", not "10 Jan 2026", "10 Jan '26", "Jan 10th, 2026", etc). In tables this may be reduced to YMD (year-month-day) to save space (e.g., "2026-01-10"). Currency Articles should always include the latest information. If something is changed in an update, it should be put in the History section and otherwise removed. Navigation v t e Policies Community Wiki rules Editing Style guide Notability Contributing
